content.text:
Done. All three renders are complete and verified.

**Files produced** (in the working folder):
- `square.png` — 1080×1080 (master)
- `landscape.png` — 1920×1080
- `story.png` — 1080×1920
- `card.html` — the single responsive source; each size is a media-query branch keyed off aspect ratio

**How it's built**
- Inter loaded via `@font-face` from the local variable TTF (weight range 100–900).
- One DOM, three layouts:
  - **Square** — brand / speaker row / big title / meta + button, with leftover space split into identical 124px gaps for even vertical rhythm.
  - **Landscape** — brand across the top, then a two-column split: portrait + name on the left, title and footer vertically centred to the right of a hairline rule.
  - **Story** — fully stacked, portrait enlarged to 520px, title at 90px, meta and button stacked left-aligned.
  - The wrappers collapse with `display:contents` in the square/story branches so the flex parent can distribute spacing across all four blocks directly.
- Portrait is a true circle at every size (fixed square box + `border-radius:50%` + `object-fit:cover`, face kept on centre with `object-position:50% 43%`), ringed in the violet accent.

**Verification** — I scripted a headless check at each exact viewport that measured every element's box. Results: portrait is exactly square-boxed (250/372/520px) so the circle never distorts; the title wraps to 3/3/5 lines and fits its column at all sizes; zero out-of-bounds elements and zero pairwise overlaps. The one clipping report is `.card` itself, which is intentional — it hides the decorative violet glow blobs that bleed past the canvas edge; no content is affected.

Two defects found and fixed along the way: in the first landscape pass the event name collided with the talk title (the brand sat inside an undersized left column), which I fixed by promoting the brand to its own full-width top row; and all three sizes had a large dead band between the speaker block and the title, resolved by flattening the wrappers and scaling type/portrait up per format.
